film: Spirited Away (Sen to Chihiro no kamikakushi)
methodology: Counts are corpus-derived from the full Japanese script (1,251 lines tagged by speaker and addressee). Each scene groups all lines within the listed dyad(s). 'desu/masu' counts teineigo predicates (ます + です stems); 'Honorific cluster' counts keigo-proper forms (ございます, sonkeigo verbs, kenjōgo verbs); 'Plain lines' counts utterances with zero polite markers. Use these tables to justify the formality, socialDistance, and zTarget settings on the graph links you are arguing about.

scenes.title: Yubaba's office — contract and name theft (Chihiro ↔ Yubaba)
scenes.dialogueFocus: Chihiro's repeated 働かせてください requests against Yubaba's zero-load command register across 72 lines.
scenes.rationale: 98 lines total; 87 are plain or rough. Chihiro's politeness is sparse and instrumental — she deploys ください at critical pressure points (five repetitions of 働かせてください) and falls back to plain speech everywhere else. Yubaba produces zero polite markers across 72 lines: sovereign command register requires no upward deferral. The asymmetry encodes maximum institutional distance.

scenes.title: Bathhouse desk — BandaiKaeru's role-bound keigo (BandaiKaeru ↔ Yubaba, Chihiro → BandaiKaeru)
scenes.dialogueFocus: Service-role keigo: every line in this 6-line cluster carries a polite marker — the most consistent load density in the corpus.
scenes.rationale: BandaiKaeru's morning ritual (おはようございます、よくお休みになられましたか？) and Chihiro's desk interaction (ありがとうございます) produce zero plain lines. The よくお休みになられましたか？ line uses double-honorification (なられる + ました) that the regex only partially captures — the true keigo load is higher than counted. This is the corpus's clearest example of role-bound keigo: register is dictated entirely by service context, not personal relationship.

scenes.title: Haku reports to Yubaba (Haku → Yubaba)
scenes.dialogueFocus: Institutional subordinate register: formal syntax carrying ultimatum-level content.
scenes.rationale: 8 of 9 lines carry polite markers. Haku opens with お呼びですか？ (pure service deference) and closes with 千と両親を人間の世界に戻してください — a demand framed as a formal request. The same register that signals submission to Yubaba is turned into a negotiating tool. This is the corpus's clearest case of formal syntax carrying defiant semantics.

scenes.title: Boiler room — Chihiro and Kamaji (Chihiro ↔ Kamaji)
scenes.dialogueFocus: Chihiro's most formally loaded single line in the corpus (ありがとうございました, load=4) toward Kamaji, not Yubaba.
scenes.rationale: The honorific cluster count of 6 is inflated by Kamaji's 待ちなさい commands (×2) — morphologically sonkeigo but pragmatically downward authority, a known なさい false positive. Chihiro's ありがとうございました (gozaimasu-class + masu = load 4) is the highest-load line she produces anywhere in the corpus, higher than anything she says to Yubaba. Genuine gratitude to a helper generates more formal register than performed deference to a sovereign.

scenes.title: Zeniba's cottage at Swamp Bottom (Chihiro ↔ Zeniba)
scenes.dialogueFocus: Chihiro's most sustained polite register in the film; Zeniba speaks to her almost entirely as a peer.
scenes.rationale: 69 lines total. Chihiro produces 11 polite-load lines across 25 utterances — her highest-density polite window — using formal apology and return-of-stolen-property speech acts (お返しに来ました、ハクの代わりに謝りに来ました). Zeniba produces 1 marker across 44 lines, addressing Chihiro with warm plain speech. The asymmetry inverts narrative rank: Zeniba's warmth and lack of ceremony reflects insider-style address toward someone she accepts as trustworthy, not condescension.

scenes.title: Chihiro ↔ Haku — intimate register (bidirectional)
scenes.dialogueFocus: The largest dyad in the corpus (152 lines); 147 of 152 in plain speech, near-perfectly symmetric.
scenes.rationale: Formality difference across 152 lines is 0.014 — effectively zero. The 5 polite markers mark transitional moments only: Haku's first rescue (かんでのみなさい), Chihiro's formal self-introduction (よろしくお願いします、千です). Once the relationship is established, both speakers converge on plain speech. The 2 keigo markers from Haku are both なさい commands — morphologically honorific, pragmatically instructive — not genuine upward deferral. This dyad anchors the low end of the formality and socialDistance scales.

mappingToGraph.linkDistance: Base spring length = 6 + 2.2×formality + 0.9×socialDistance; honorificLinkMetrics.js subtracts 2.6×hierarchySalience so power-relevant upward-deferral dyads sit slightly closer in 3D.
mappingToGraph.linkStrength: d3 link spring strength = 0.3 + hierarchySalience×0.52; salient hierarchy edges pull the layout tighter.
mappingToGraph.edgeDrawing: Line width, opacity, dash size, and crawl speed all scale with formality, socialDistance, and hierarchySalience. A directed arrowhead cone at the target node shows which party is the addressee.
mappingToGraph.zAxis: Node zTarget drives forceZ (orthogonal to basePower on forceY). Negative zTarget = uchi (institutional insiders, e.g. Yubaba at −4); positive = soto (outsiders, e.g. Chihiro's parents at +3). See the Z-depth indicator below the node cluster in the 3D view.
